thread:
sara_support: Hey team, large customer (DataLens) just escalated — after yesterday's reranker rollout their retrieval-based answers are much worse: worse grounding, citations missing or wrong, recall dropped on their eval set. Ticket #CS-8421. They provided reproducible example and request IDs.

sara_support: Example query they sent: "list the three latest SEC filings mentioning 'related-party transactions' for company X". Our endpoint returned 0 matches and instead hallucinated a citation to an unrelated doc. Repro steps they gave: call /v1/retrieve with top_k=50, reranker=on (default), then generate. They included request_id: req_20260315_9b2f.

maria_cs: Ugh. Did they say this coincided with the "reranker weight adjustment" rollout last night?

sara_support: Yes — they saw the change start ~2026-03-14T22:10Z which matches the deploy window.

andrew_eng: @lee_oncall can you pull the canary vs global metrics? specifically: reranker score distributions, top1 precision@k, and embedding similarity histograms for queries in their project. Also fetch the exact model variant used in the live route for that org (hosted vs dedicated?).

lee_oncall: On it. Quick findings: canary had a 0.12 mean shift down in reranker_score and an increase in queries returning empty hits (top_k matches with score < threshold). Their org is on hosted RW inference (model pinned to v3.2) but reranker config was rolled as a platform-level change (weight parameter moved from 0.8 -> 0.45 by default). I have a screenshot of the score histogram and a trace id: trace_3fa9b.

oliver_research: That weight change would definitely reduce grounding — if reranker weight dropped, generation relies more on LM and less on retrieved contexts, causing hallucination and worse citations. We also changed the default similarity metric in the rollout (cosine -> dot-product for speed) in the same PR (hash: a1b2c3). Could be both.

chris_ml: I ran a quick local repro against their sample queries using pre-rollout config (weight=0.8, cosine) and post-rollout (weight=0.45, dot). Results: recall@10 went from 0.82 -> 0.53, and grounded citation rate dropped similarly. Pasted sample calls below: 
```http
POST /v1/retrieve
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "org_id":"datalens",
  "query":"list the three latest SEC filings mentioning 'related-party_transactions' for company X",
  "top_k":50,
  "embedding_model":"embed-large-v2",
  "reranker_config": {"type":"cross-encoder","weight":0.45,"similarity":"dot"}
}
```

chris_ml: And this is the working config that matches pre-rollout: 
```json
{"reranker_config":{"weight":0.8,"similarity":"cosine"}}
```

maria_cs: Customer is asking for an ETA to fix — they need reliable citations for a demo next week. They asked whether we can rollback for just their org.

andrew_eng: Two immediate remediation options: 1) Rollback the platform-level defaults to previous values (weight 0.8, cosine) globally — fastest but more disruption. 2) Hotfix to allow per-org override so we can pin DataLens back to pre-rollout defaults (safer). We should also add a canary alert for large shifts in reranker_score distribution.

lee_oncall: I can patch route config to add org-specific override for DataLens and pin reranker weight back to 0.8 and similarity to cosine. Will need a short maintenance window to apply and validate. I'll also re-run dataset-level eval (their provided prompt set) after change.

sara_support: Customer prefers option 2 (pin for them) first. Can we do an emergency patch? Also they asked if this affects historical indexes — could a similarity metric change require reindexing?

oliver_research: Dot vs cosine on normalized embeddings is equivalent up to scaling, but if embeddings aren't L2-normalized then switching metric can change neighbor ordering. If their index was built assuming cosine (normalized vectors) and rollout used raw dot without normalizing, recall suffers. Reindexing with the new metric normalization flag or restoring metric should fix ordering. We should inspect index metadata: normalization flag, distance type.

andrew_eng: Action plan: 1) @lee_oncall apply org override and pin reranker config for DataLens (ETA 45m). 2) @chris_ml + @oliver_research run local eval against customer's prompt set to verify fix. 3) If fix passes, notify customer and keep monitoring. 4) Postmortem on rollout: missing canary guard and metric migration note.

lee_oncall: Starting patch now. I'll post logs.

alertbot: Deploy started for config-patch-20260315 by lee_oncall at 2026-03-15T01:12:10Z.

lee_oncall: Patch applied for org=datalens: reranker.weight=0.8, reranker.similarity=cosine. Verified route returned expected hits for their sample query. Trace: trace_3fa9b -> trace_3fb0c.

chris_ml: Re-ran eval with the customer's 120-query suite against the patched config: recall@10 recovered to 0.80 (previously 0.53). Citations look correct now. Attaching top example diffs in the ticket.

maria_cs: Customer confirmed improvement in their staging tests and asked us to keep the override until they finish their demo next week. They've asked for a permanent opt-in in Console to prefer "preference: stronger_reranker_grounding".

andrew_eng: Filed follow-up work: add per-org reranker knobs in Console + migration checklist for changing similarity metric + automated detection + rollback playbook. I'll open ENG issues and link to CS ticket #CS-8421.

sara_support: Thank you all — I'll update the customer and close the urgent escalation once they confirm after tomorrow's run. :tada:

lee_oncall: Leaving notes in the incident channel and adding a short blameless postmortem template.

oliver_research: Also recommend we run a sampled audit across top customers to detect regression risk whenever we change reranker defaults.

maria_cs: Noted. Customer appreciated the quick turnaround.

sara_support: Closing loop for now. If the customer sees any residual hallucinations, escalate back here with request_id and a sample query. Thanks!
